questions.question:
The line $y = mx$ is a tangent to the curve $y = \cos x$ at the point where $x = a$, as shown in the diagram.

Which of the following statements is true?
questions.answer:
**B.** From the diagram the point of contact is just before the maximum at $x = 2\pi$, so $a < 2\pi$ and hence $\dfrac{1}{a} > \dfrac{1}{2\pi}$.

At $x = a$ the line meets the curve: $ma = \cos a < 1$, so $m < \dfrac{1}{a}$.

Near $x = a$ the curve is concave down, so the tangent lies above it; at $x = 2\pi$ the line is above $\cos 2\pi = 1$, i.e. $2\pi m > 1$, so $m > \dfrac{1}{2\pi}$.

Therefore $\dfrac{1}{2\pi} < m < \dfrac{1}{a}$.

questions.question:
Frat is on a swing whose base is 10 metres away from a 1200 W speaker. The speaker plays music such that its loudness, $\beta$ decibels, is given by
$$\beta = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{10^{-12}}\right), \quad \text{where } I = \frac{P}{r^{2}},$$
$P$ is the power of the sound source in watts, and $r$ is the distance in metres between the source and the observer.

Frat starts swinging 1 metre away from the base of the swing, so that he is 11 m from the speaker. He then swings so that his horizontal displacement after $t$ seconds is sinusoidal, and he completes 3 swings in 7 seconds. Frat swings directly towards and away from the speaker.

Show that $r = 10 + \cos\left(\dfrac{6\pi}{7}t\right)$, where $t$ is in seconds.
questions.answer:
Period $= \dfrac{7}{3}$ s, so $b = \dfrac{2\pi}{7/3} = \dfrac{6\pi}{7}$.

The distance oscillates about the base (10 m) with amplitude 1 m, so $r = 10 + a\cos(bt)$ with $a = 1$ (since $r = 11$ when $t = 0$, a cosine with no phase shift).

$$r = 10 + \cos\left(\frac{6\pi}{7}t\right)$$
questions.author: Haysen

$$\beta = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{10^{-12}}\right), \quad \text{where } I = \frac{P}{r^{2}},$$
$P$ is the power of the sound source in watts, and $r$ is the distance in metres between the source and the observer.
